item.title: CRD and Policy Model
item.description:
The contract between Joulie’s components: pods state demand, node labels expose supply, NodeHardware publishes what a node is, and NodeTwin carries what it should be. Use this page to read or debug these objects.

APIs
Group and version joulie.io/v1alpha1
CRDs NodeHardware (nodehardwares), NodeTwin (nodetwins), both cluster-scoped
Definitions config/crd/bases/joulie.io_nodehardwares.yaml, config/crd/bases/joulie.io_nodetwins.yaml

Demand model (workloads)

Demand comes from the joulie.io/workload-class pod annotation:

  • performance: the pod carries joulie.io/workload-class: performance and is kept off eco and draining nodes.
  • standard (default): no annotation, or standard. It can run on any node; scoring steers it toward eco when performance nodes are congested.

Supply model (nodes)

Signal Values Set by
node label joulie.io/power-profile performance, eco controller manager
NodeTwin.status.schedulableClass performance, eco, draining controller manager (twin)

draining is the transition safeguard while a node moves toward eco with performance pods still on it; the scheduler extender filters it out for performance pods. schedulableClass is internal: users express placement intent only with the pod annotation.

item.title: Joulie Controller Manager
item.description:
The controller manager is Joulie’s cluster-level decision engine: it decides which nodes supply performance capacity and which can safely supply eco, and publishes that through Kubernetes objects and labels. It never writes host power interfaces; the agent does.

Responsibilities

Part Runs Does
Twin controller every RECONCILE_INTERVAL (1 min) reads measured power and NodeHardware, writes the twin’s scores to NodeTwin.status (Digital Twin)
Policy controller every RECONCILE_INTERVAL classifies demand, runs the policy, applies the downgrade guard, writes NodeTwin.spec (caps and, with governor control on, governor presets) and the joulie.io/power-profile label
Facility poller every FACILITY_POLL_INTERVAL (30 s), off by default reads ambient temperatures, IT, cooling and rack power, carbon intensity (Measured inputs)

The controller manager decides what each node should be; the agent decides how to apply it on the node.

item.title: Joulie Agent
item.description:
The agent is Joulie’s node-side component: it discovers the node’s hardware and applies the caps and governor presets the controller manager plans. It does not plan policy.

Responsibilities

Every reconcile (RECONCILE_INTERVAL, 20 s), for each node it owns, the agent:

Step What
1 discovers CPU and GPU hardware, cap ranges and governors
2 publishes them as NodeHardware
3 reads the desired state in NodeTwin.spec
4 applies the governor presets and the CPU and GPU caps, through host interfaces or HTTP
5 reports the outcome in NodeTwin.status.controlStatus and on /metrics

Inputs and outputs

Inputs Outputs
NodeTwin.spec: profile, caps, governor presets NodeHardware: discovered hardware and capabilities
backend variables (TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE, TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL, TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL; default host) writes to RAPL, cpufreq and GPU interfaces, or the simulator over HTTP
node labels (hardware identity, NFD and GPU feature discovery) NodeTwin.status.controlStatus: applied, blocked, error or none per component
Prometheus metrics on /metrics (Metrics Reference)

NodeHardware is the agent’s output; you do not write it.

item.title: Digital Twin
item.description:
The digital twin turns each node’s measured power and hardware limits into a few scores the scheduler and the policy use. It is a closed-form model in the controller manager (pkg/controller/twin), computed every reconcile, and its output is NodeTwin.status.

What the digital twin computes

Field in NodeTwin.status Meaning Range Read by
predictedPowerHeadroomScore share of the node’s capped power budget still unused up to 100, negative when over budget scheduler (fallback)
predictedCoolingStressScore measured power over node TDP, scaled up in warm ambient air 0 to 100 scheduler
predictedPsuStressScore rack (or cluster) power over a 50 kW reference capacity 0 to 100 nobody yet
estimatedPUE cooling stress restated on a PUE scale 1.05 to 1.40 nobody yet
schedulableClass performance, eco or draining scheduler, controller manager
powerMeasurement measured power, TDP, capped budget and trend, per node watts scheduler
conditions AgentReporting: whether an agent enforces the caps the Agent column of kubectl get nodetwins

Every power score starts from the measured node power powerMeasurement.measuredNodePowerW, not from the caps.

item.title: Policy Algorithms
item.description:
A policy decides how many managed nodes run the performance profile; every other node runs eco. Pick one with POLICY_TYPE on the controller manager. The policies are in pkg/controller/policy/.

Demand is the number of pods annotated joulie.io/workload-class: performance; pods without the annotation are standard.

Which performance nodes

static_partition and queue_aware_v1 compute a count; the controller manager then splits it across hardware families (gpu:<model>, cpu:<model>) in proportion to family size, at least one node per family, keeping nodes already in performance first. A change of one in the count moves exactly one node. The split is exported as joulie_policy_family_nodes{family} and joulie_policy_family_performance_nodes{family}.

item.title: Scheduler Extender
item.description:
Joulie’s scheduler extender keeps performance pods off eco nodes and ranks the remaining nodes by power headroom and cooling stress. It is an HTTP extender that kube-scheduler calls; it does not replace kube-scheduler. The chart always deploys it; without it pods get standard Kubernetes scheduling.

How a pod gets scheduled (end-to-end)

  1. kube-scheduler picks up the new pod and runs its own filters (resources, taints, affinity).
  2. It calls Joulie’s POST /filter: performance pods lose the eco and draining nodes.
  3. It calls POST /prioritize: Joulie scores each remaining node 0 to 100 for this pod and returns it as a 0 to 10 priority.
  4. kube-scheduler adds Joulie’s priority, times the extender weight, to its own plugin scores and binds the pod to the best node.

Placement intent comes from one pod annotation, joulie.io/workload-class, so users write no scheduling rules. The extender does not migrate or evict pods and never overrides resource fits.

item.title: Energy-Aware Scheduling
item.description:
This page follows one placement decision from the hardware counters to the chosen node. Each stage is a separate component that hands its result to the next through Prometheus or a CRD, and each links to the page that documents it.

End-to-end pipeline

RAPL/NVML readings as OpenTelemetry metrics (or Kepler)
 -> Prometheus (OTLP receiver, or scrape)
 -> Digital twin (NodeTwin.status)
 -> Scheduler extender (filter + score)
 -> Placement decision

Stage 1: Telemetry collection

CPU (RAPL) and GPU (NVML, ROCm SMI) power reach Prometheus as the OpenTelemetry metrics hw.energy and hw.power, or through Kepler: Input metrics (OpenTelemetry).

item.title: Input Telemetry and Actuation Interfaces
item.description:
How Joulie reads power and facility telemetry, and how the agent sends its control intents. Use it to wire Prometheus, an OpenTelemetry producer or the simulator to Joulie. Exported /metrics are on the Metrics Reference; the CRD fields are on CRD and Policy Model.

Backends

The same control logic runs on real hardware and on simulator or KWOK clusters; environment variables on the agent choose the wiring, never the hardware identity (that is NodeHardware).

item.title: Metrics Reference
item.description:
Every Prometheus metric the agent, the controller manager and the scheduler extender export, for dashboards and alerts. Simulator metrics are on Simulator Metrics; the metrics Joulie reads as input are on Input Telemetry and Actuation Interfaces.

Endpoints by component

Component Path Default address Override
Agent /metrics :8080 METRICS_ADDR
Controller manager /metrics :8081 METRICS_ADDR
Scheduler extender /metrics :9877 METRICS_ADDR

Agent metrics

Backend and selected cap

  • joulie_backend_mode{node,mode} (gauge)
    • mode: none|rapl|dvfs
    • active mode is 1, others 0
  • joulie_policy_cap_watts{node,policy} (gauge)
    • current selected policy cap in watts

RAPL power/energy

  • joulie_rapl_energy_uj{node,zone} (gauge)
    • latest raw RAPL energy counter in microjoules
  • joulie_rapl_estimated_power_watts{node,zone} (gauge)
    • per-zone estimated power from energy deltas
  • joulie_rapl_package_total_power_watts{node} (gauge)
    • sum of package-level estimated power

DVFS controller

  • joulie_dvfs_observed_power_watts{node} (gauge)
    • observed package power used by DVFS controller
  • joulie_dvfs_ema_power_watts{node} (gauge)
    • EMA-smoothed power used for decisions
  • joulie_dvfs_throttle_pct{node} (gauge)
    • current throttle percentage
  • joulie_dvfs_above_trip_count{node} (gauge)
    • consecutive above-threshold samples
  • joulie_dvfs_below_trip_count{node} (gauge)
    • consecutive below-threshold samples
  • joulie_dvfs_actions_total{node,action} (counter)
    • action: throttle_up|throttle_down

CPU frequency observability

  • joulie_dvfs_cpu_cur_freq_khz{node,cpu} (gauge)
    • current CPU/policy frequency in kHz
  • joulie_dvfs_cpu_max_freq_khz{node,cpu} (gauge)
    • enforced max frequency cap in kHz

Governors

Written by the agent’s governor control.
